question: A warehouse operates throughout the day. They start with 96 items. They lose 69 items to morning shipment. They add 55 items from afternoon delivery. They lose 2 items to damage. They multiply by 5 to forecast five days. They divide by 5 for five loading zones. They lose 47 items to afternoon orders. Converting to units, what is their final count?

A business starts with 13 dollars in the morning. They add 46 dollars from early sales. They add 41 dollars from additional revenue. They multiply by 7 to project for seven days. By evening, they lose 454 dollars to operating costs. How much is left after daily operations?

A warehouse operates throughout the day. They start with 100 items. Sarah and Tom compare inventory. They lose 72 items to morning shipment. They multiply by 5 to forecast five days. They add 62 items from afternoon delivery. They lose 4 items to damage. They multiply by 4 to project weekly. Converting to dozens, what is their weekly forecast?

A store operates throughout the day. They start with 79 items in stock. They lose 56 items to morning sales. They add 52 items from delivery. They multiply by 5 to forecast five days. They lose 186 items to a large order. They add 29 items from returns. They double by 2 for weekly planning. What is their weekly forecast?

A student starts with 16 study pages. Jacob and Nicole compare their work. They double by 2 through reviewing. They multiply by 6 to prepare for six exams. They lose 77 pages to consolidation. They add 60 pages of new material. They add 15 pages from practice. They lose 179 pages to completion. What is their final study material?

A business starts with 125 items. They double by 2 through expansion. They multiply by 4 to forecast four quarters. They add 38 items from new inventory. They lose 294 items to sales. They lose 448 items to a large order. The facility has 22 workers. What is their final count?

A workshop starts with 66 items. They divide by 2 for two workstations. They lose 1 item to breakage. They divide by 2 again for two shifts. They multiply by 3 to triple for overflow. They lose 19 items to wear. The shop opened 8 years ago. What is their final inventory?

A production line operates through the day. They start with 25 units in the morning. In the morning, they lose 7 units to quality issues. By mid-day, they multiply by 7 to scale production. By afternoon, they multiply by 6 to prepare for six shipments. By evening, they add 78 units from recovery. What is their final daily production?

A factory operates throughout the day. They start with 58 units in the morning. They multiply by 7 to project for seven days. They lose 332 units to fulfillment. They add 13 units from recovery. They lose 15 units to defects. They multiply by 9 to forecast nine weeks. Converting to hundreds, what is their nine-week forecast?

A business operates through the day. They start with 24 dollars in the morning. They multiply by 9 to scale revenue. They add 59 dollars from sales. They multiply by 7 to project weekly. They add 43 dollars from additional income. They add 35 dollars from interest. Converting to cents, what is their weekly total?

A student starts with 44 points. Michael and Rachel compare their scores. They lose 21 points to a failed quiz. They lose 19 points to a missed assignment. They lose 2 points to a rounding error. They add 7 points from extra credit. They multiply by 3 to project final grade. They multiply by 9 to forecast next semester. What is their next semester projection?

A workshop operates throughout the day. They start with 38 items in the morning. They lose 21 items to orders. They add 34 items from delivery. They lose 37 items to a correction. They multiply by 6 to forecast six weeks. They multiply by 7 to project for seven weeks. How many items do they project?

A factory operates throughout the day. They start with 100 units in production. They multiply by 4 to scale for four shifts. They add 59 units from overflow. They multiply by 4 to forecast four weeks. They lose 1438 units to fulfillment. They lose 187 units to quality control. Converting to dozens, what is their four-week total?

A warehouse operates throughout the day. They start with 189 items in the morning. They multiply by 9 to forecast nine days. They add 51 items from delivery. They lose 1149 items to large orders. They add 71 items from recovery. They multiply by 3 to project quarterly. They multiply by 6 for six-month planning. Converting to hundreds, what is their six-month forecast?

A company operates through the day. They start with 209 dollars in the morning. They multiply by 2 to double through matching funds. They lose 171 dollars to costs. They multiply by 3 to project for three months. They lose 133 dollars to taxes. They add 79 dollars from interest. Converting to cents, what is their three-month total?

A business starts with 85 items. Kevin and Michelle compare their inventory. They add 25 items from delivery. They lose 25 items to sales. They add 43 items from returns. They multiply by 5 to forecast five days. The manager has worked 18 years. What is their five-day forecast?

A warehouse operates through the day. They start with 226 items in the morning. They multiply by 9 to forecast nine weeks. They lose 1686 items to major orders. They add 45 items from recovery. They lose 269 items to damage. They multiply by 7 to project for seven weeks. Converting to hundreds, what is their seven-week forecast?

A business operates through the day. They start with 138 dollars in the morning. Daniel and Lisa compare their finances. They multiply by 7 to project for seven months. They lose 728 dollars to expenses. They lose 229 dollars to taxes. They multiply by 3 to triple for fiscal planning. They add 62 dollars from bonuses. The company opened 10 years ago. What is their annual projection?

A student starts with 210 items to study. They multiply by 3 for triple review. They divide by 5 for five study groups. They divide by 3 again to split among three partners. They multiply by 8 to prepare for eight exams. They add 52 items from additional material. Converting to dozens, how many items per exam?

A warehouse operates throughout the day. They start with 90 items in the morning. They lose 35 items to orders. They multiply by 5 to forecast five days. They add 47 items from delivery. They add 43 items from recovery. They multiply by 3 to project for three weeks. They lose 516 items to fulfillment. What is their three-week forecast?

An investor tracks their portfolio. They start with 14 dollars. Jason and Nicole compare accounts. They divide by 2 to split between two funds. They add 52 dollars from new investments. They multiply by 8 to project for eight months. They add 21 dollars from dividends. What is their eight-month projection?

A collection starts with 185 items. They lose 1 item to removal. They add 17 items from acquisition. They add 18 items from donation. They lose 7 items to discarding. They lose 53 items to redistribution. Converting to dozens, how many items remain?

A business operates through the day. They start with 184 dollars in the morning. They lose 80 dollars to opening costs. They double by 2 through morning sales. They add 59 dollars from additional revenue. They add 76 dollars from other sources. They add 15 dollars in interest. Converting to dollars, what is their daily total?

Sarah had 209 cents. She spent 2 cents on a pencil. Then she found 8 cents in a coat pocket. Her grandmother gave her 7 cents. She earned 4 cents for helping at home. Finally, she spent 68 cents, which converts to just under 1 dollar, on a small toy. Yesterday she saw a bike that cost 150 dollars but wasn't interested. How much money does Sarah have left in cents?

A bookshelf started with 198 books. During spring cleanup, 166 books were donated to the library. Then Maya bought 78 used books from a garage sale. Later, 49 books were lent to a school, leaving them temporarily. Her family donated 68 books they found in the attic. Finally, 54 books were removed for recycling, and 16 new books were added. The living room had space for 200 more books (but that doesn't affect the count). How many books are on the bookshelf now?
